title: EU online consumer adoption is expanding faster than protection, trust, and sustainable-choice capacity
source_unit: European Commission Consumer Conditions Scoreboard 2025 and November 2024 Consumer Conditions Survey
geography: EU27 plus Iceland and Norway; representative consumer survey across the Single Market

observations.period: 2024 Consumer Conditions Survey; online commerce, cost pressure, and purchase problems

denominator.unit: representative consumers in EU27 Member States plus Iceland and Norway; survey sample size not stated in the scoreboard report

online_consumer_share.unit: percent of consumers buying online, up from 71% in 2022

online_crossborder_eu.unit: percent buying from another EU country in 2024, up from 27% in 2022

online_purchase_problem.unit: percent of online buyers experiencing a problem they felt gave legitimate reason to complain

offline_purchase_problem.unit: percent of offline buyers experiencing a problem they felt gave legitimate reason to complain

bill_payment_concern.unit: percent concerned about being able to pay bills

preferred_food_affordability_concern.unit: percent worried about affording preferred food

mechanism.value: Digital consumer reach and cross-border choice are expanding while problem exposure and household budget pressure remain materially higher online or at the point of everyday consumption

observations.method: European Commission Consumer Conditions Survey conducted in November 2024 by Ipsos for the Commission; the Scoreboard combines survey results with contextual data and compares selected indicators with 2022.
observations.uncertainty: The online/offline problem comparison is descriptive and does not identify whether platform complexity, product mix, consumer expectations, reporting propensity, or purchase frequency causes the difference; the survey does not establish household welfare.
observations.subgroup: Consumers in EU27, Iceland, and Norway; online and offline purchasers have different conditional denominators.
observations.counterinterpretation: Online shoppers may report more problems because they transact more often, have more visible complaint routes, or buy more cross-border—not necessarily because every online transaction is intrinsically less reliable.

observations.period: 2024 Consumer Conditions Survey; digital fairness, scams, and unfair commercial practices

denominator.unit: consumers who buy online for targeted-advertising measures; all surveyed consumers for scam and unfair-practice measures

targeted_advertising_concern.unit: percent of online buyers worried about online targeted advertising

personal_data_consent_concern.unit: percent of online buyers concerned about personal-data collection without consent

excessive_advertising_concern.unit: percent of online buyers concerned about excessive advertising

unavoidable_personalisation_concern.unit: percent of online buyers concerned about unavoidable personalisation

online_scams.unit: percent encountering fraudulent practices or scams online

fake_reviews.unit: percent encountering or noticing fake reviews as an unfair online practice

misleading_discounting.unit: percent encountering or noticing misleading discounting

mechanism.value: Consumer attention and data are being used in a market where perceived manipulation, fraud, reputation distortion, and discount opacity are widespread enough to become a trust problem rather than isolated incidents

observations.method: Scoreboard survey estimates for online targeted-advertising concerns and consumer-reported online fraud and unfair commercial practices.
observations.uncertainty: The measures capture experience or perception, not verified fraud incidence, monetary loss, platform responsibility, or causal effects on purchasing; conditional denominators differ by question.
observations.subgroup: Online buyers for advertising measures; the broader surveyed consumer population for scam and unfair-practice measures.
observations.counterinterpretation: High awareness of fake reviews or scams could reflect effective consumer vigilance as well as high exposure; perceived unfairness does not prove legal infringement in each case.

observations.period: 2024 Consumer Conditions Survey; sustainability, repair, and institutional trust

denominator.unit: EU27 consumers in the representative Consumer Conditions Survey; subgroup denominators vary by question

environmental_purchase_influence.unit: percent factoring environmental impact into at least one or two recent purchases, down 13 percentage points from 2022

replace_defective_product.unit: percent replacing a defective product with a new one

secondhand_refurbished_replacement.unit: percent buying second-hand or refurbished as a replacement

repair_cost_barrier.unit: percent of non-repairers citing cost as a reason not to repair

repair_effort_barrier.unit: percent of non-repairers citing effort as a reason not to repair

trust_public_protection.unit: percent agreeing that public organisations protect consumer rights

trust_traders.unit: percent agreeing that retailers and service providers respect consumer rights

mechanism.value: Cost and effort suppress repair and sustainable choice even as consumers express trust in traders and public protection; formal confidence does not automatically convert into lower-waste behavior or effective remedy

observations.method: Scoreboard estimates on sustainable purchasing, defective-product response, barriers to repair, and trust in traders and public organisations.
observations.uncertainty: The survey does not establish whether price, convenience, availability, product quality, knowledge, or infrastructure causes the observed sustainable-choice decline; repair measures are self-reported and conditional.
observations.subgroup: EU27 consumers, with repair barriers conditional on consumers who did not repair a defective product.
observations.counterinterpretation: The fall in environmental purchasing may partly reflect question framing, changing product mix, or reduced salience rather than a durable rejection of sustainability; trust can coexist with skepticism about individual firms.

related_sources.claim: The European Commission summary identifies the 2025 Consumer Conditions Scoreboard, its November 2024 representative survey, and its headline online-problem, scam, cost-of-living, trust, and sustainability findings.
The Commission provides the underlying 2024 survey data by country/region and demographic group as downloadable datasets.

boundary: This record adds EU-wide consumer-conditions evidence connecting e-commerce growth to purchase problems, scams, fake reviews, targeted-ad concerns, cost-of-living pressure, repair barriers, sustainable-choice decline, and institutional trust. It does not provide verified fraud loss, household welfare, causal effects, platform-level attribution, or a single common denominator for all conditional indicators.
